tells.name: The first screen does not say what this is or what to do
tells.summary: A new user cannot tell, within five seconds, what the product does for them and what to do first.

tells.name: A marketing page in front of the tool
tells.summary: People who come to use the product land on a sales page and have to find a Get Started button to reach their work.

detectors.note: A hero section in the app's own routes. Legitimate on a marketing site, so the reviewer confirms.

tells.name: A dashboard of zeros or invented numbers for a new user
tells.summary: The first screen after sign-up is a grid of charts and counters that are empty or made up, instead of the first step of the job.

tells.name: Navigation that mirrors the database
tells.summary: The menu lists tables (Contacts, Triggers, Tags, Sequences) as equal peers instead of the jobs people come to do.

tells.name: Features that do not exist yet
tells.summary: Menu items, cards or buttons that lead to Coming soon, a disabled page or nothing at all.

tells.name: More features than the job needs
tells.summary: Dashboards, reports, templates and settings built around a product whose users come for one or two jobs. Every extra screen is one more place to get lost.

tells.name: Dead buttons and fake links
tells.summary: Buttons and links that look real but go nowhere: href="#", empty handlers, or handlers that only log or alert.

tells.name: Everything asked up front
tells.summary: A single form asks for every field the data model has before the person gets anything back.

detectors.note: Forms with seven or more fields.

tells.name: A modal for everything
tells.summary: Creating, editing and viewing all happen in dialogs that cover the context, lose work on a stray click and cannot be linked to.

tells.name: A dead end after success
tells.summary: After finishing a task the person gets a toast and an unchanged screen, with no sign of what happened or what to do next.

tells.name: Sign-up or setup before the first result
tells.summary: An account, API keys, integrations or a long onboarding come before the person sees the product do anything.

phrases: log in to your account to
sign in to your account to
detectors.note: Sign-up walls, login walls and credential fields. Legitimate in developer tools, so the reviewer confirms.

tells.name: Confirmation for safe actions
tells.summary: Are you sure? dialogs on actions that are easy to undo, which trains people to click through the one that matters.

hit: Are you sure you want to continue?

tells.name: A wizard for a one-screen task
tells.summary: A stepper splits a short task into several screens with one or two fields each.

detectors.note: A next-step handler. Catches wizards that show their steps as numbered circles.

tells.name: Losing your place
tells.summary: Opening or editing an item resets filters, scroll or the selected tab, and there is no clear way back.

tells.name: Options the system could decide
tells.summary: The form asks for things with an obvious answer: a status, a delay, a currency, the only account or the only branch. Each one is a decision the person should not have to make.

tells.name: Two ways to do the same thing
tells.summary: Different buttons or pages start the same job with different labels or different results, so people cannot tell which one is the real path.

tells.name: Personal data the job does not use
tells.summary: Forms ask for a tax id, a birth date, a gender or how the person found you when the task does not use any of it.

detectors.note: A tax id can be legitimate for invoices, so the reviewer confirms the task needs it.
The Brazilian tax id as the person reads it, in a label or placeholder. An optional CPF for the receipt (CPF na nota) is a normal request, so it does not count.

tells.name: Asking for the same thing twice
tells.summary: Confirm your e-mail, confirm your password: fields that make people type again what they just typed.

tells.name: The main action far from what it acts on
tells.summary: The button that starts the job sits in a far corner of the header while the content it acts on is somewhere else.

tells.name: Several primary buttons competing
tells.summary: More than one filled, colored or gradient button in view, so nothing tells the person which step comes next.

tells.name: Icon-only buttons with no name
tells.summary: Buttons that show only an icon, with no visible label, tooltip or accessible name.

detectors.note: A button whose only child is an icon component and that has no aria-label or title.

tells.name: Destructive actions that look safe
tells.summary: Delete sits next to Edit with the same style and no undo, so a slip destroys work.

tells.name: Actions that only appear on hover
tells.summary: Row or card actions stay invisible until the pointer hovers, so touch users never see them and others have to hunt.

tells.name: The same action in a different place on each screen
tells.summary: Save is at the top on one screen and at the bottom on the next, and the main button swaps sides between dialogs.

tells.name: Disabled buttons that do not say why
tells.summary: The submit button stays grey until something is right, and nothing says what is missing.

tells.name: Targets too small to tap
tells.summary: Buttons and links smaller than 24 by 24 pixels, often tiny icon buttons packed together.

tells.name: Fields named only by their placeholder
tells.summary: The only name a field has is the gray hint inside it, and it disappears as soon as the person starts typing.

detectors.note: A field with a placeholder, no id or aria-label, and no label right before it. A label wrapped around the field is fine, so the reviewer confirms.

tells.name: Purple-to-blue gradient as the brand
tells.summary: A purple, violet or indigo gradient carries the brand instead of a color chosen for the audience.

tells.name: Gradient text
tells.summary: Headlines painted with a gradient clipped to the text.

tells.name: Glass, blur and glow
tells.summary: Frosted translucent panels, blurred color blobs behind the content and colored glows under buttons.

hit: <div className="absolute -top-20 h-72 w-72 rounded-full bg-purple-500/30 blur-3xl" />

tells.name: Everything is a card
tells.summary: Every block gets rounded corners, a border and a shadow, often cards inside cards, so nothing stands out.

tells.name: The three-card feature grid
tells.summary: Three equal cards with an icon, a two-word title and a vague sentence each.

tells.name: An icon in a tinted square for every item
tells.summary: Each item gets a decorative icon inside a pale colored square or circle, whether or not the icon helps anyone recognize it.

miss: JD

tells.name: KPI cards with invented trends
tells.summary: A row of stat cards with round numbers and green +12.5% from last month badges that no data backs.

tells.name: Emoji as icons
tells.summary: Emoji stand in for icons, bullets and headings in the interface.

tells.name: Sparkles and AI-powered badges
tells.summary: Sparkle icons and AI-powered labels decorate features that the person does not need to know are AI.

tells.name: Everything centered
tells.summary: Headings, paragraphs and whole pages are centered, which makes long text slow to read and pages look like slides.

tells.name: Motion on everything
tells.summary: Cards scale on hover, everything transitions every property, and badges bounce, so movement stops meaning anything.

tells.name: Washed-out text
tells.summary: Light gray text on white, or white text on a bright brand color, for things people need to read, below the WCAG contrast minimum.

detectors.note: Light gray on white fails contrast. On a dark theme the same classes are fine, so the detector is skipped there and the probe measures the real ratio.
White text on a bright color, or on a gradient that starts with one. These shades stay below 3 to 1 with white, so the probe confirms the ratio.

hit: <button className="rounded-xl bg-gradient-to-r from-orange-500 to-red-600 px-5 py-2.5 font-bold text-white">Adicionar</button>

tells.name: Generic value-proposition phrases
tells.summary: Stock marketing lines that fit any product and say nothing about this one.

miss: Reply to every comment with a DM

tells.name: Buttons that do not say what happens
tells.summary: Get Started, Learn More, Submit and Click here, where the label should name the result.

detectors.pattern: >\s*(?:get started|learn more|read more|submit|click here|proceed|começar|comece agora|saiba mais|leia mais|clique aqui|prosseguir)\s*<

tells.name: Invented social proof and numbers
tells.summary: Trusted by 10,000+ teams, 4.9 out of 5, and testimonials from a CEO at a company that does not exist.

detectors.note: Counts of customers or orders and star ratings with no source.

hit: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Mais de 10.000 empresas confiam no Orça Já
miss: Used every day by our support team

tells.name: Placeholder people and data left in
tells.summary: Lorem ipsum, John Doe, Acme and random avatar services in screens real people will see.

detectors.pattern: lorem ipsum|\bjohn doe\b|\bjane (?:doe|smith)\b|\bacme\b|i\.pravatar\.cc|randomuser\.me|source\.unsplash\.com|images\.unsplash\.com/photo-|placehold\.co|via\.placeholder\.com|placekitten\.com|picsum\.photos|\bfulano(?: de tal)?\b|example@(?:example|email)\.com|123 main st|\bjo[aã]o da silva\b|\bjos[eé] da silva\b|\bmaria da silva\b|\bempresa (?:xyz|abc|exemplo)\b|\b(?:ciclano|sicrano|beltrano)\b|teste@teste\.com

tells.name: Code words on screen
tells.summary: Enum values, table names and snake_case keys shown to people as labels: COMMENT_KEYWORD, flow_status, Entity.

tells.name: Stock greetings and filler
tells.summary: Welcome back, John! Here's what's happening today. Oops! Lines that take space and tell nothing.

phrases: aqui está o que está acontecendo

detectors.note: A hello and a waving hand in front of the person's name.

hit: Here's what's happening with your account today.

tells.name: Error messages that do not help
tells.summary: Something went wrong, An error occurred, Invalid input: messages that do not say what failed or what to do.

miss: We could not reach Instagram. Check your connection and try again.

tells.name: Two languages in one interface
tells.summary: A product for Portuguese speakers with Dashboard, Settings and Submit left in English, or the reverse.

tells.name: Empty states that only say no data
tells.summary: An empty list or chart says No data and stops, at the exact moment a new user needs to be told what to do.

miss: No automations yet. Create one to reply to comments automatically.

tells.name: No loading feedback
tells.summary: Buttons stay clickable and screens stay blank while work happens, or a full-page spinner hides everything for a small update.

tells.name: Errors that only reach the console
tells.summary: Failures are caught and logged, and the person sees nothing, so they wait or repeat the action.

miss: try { await save(); } catch (e) { setError(e.message); console.error(e); }

tells.name: Success that leaves no trace
tells.summary: A generic Success! toast is the only sign that something happened, with no link to the result and no undo.

detectors.note: A generic success message. The reviewer checks whether the screen also shows the result.

miss: toast.success("Automation is live. It replies to LINK on any post.");

tells.name: Breaks on a phone
tells.summary: Fixed widths and grids that never collapse push content off screen at phone sizes.

detectors.note: Grids of three or more columns with room between items and no responsive variant. Compact grids such as calendars and option chips fit on a phone.

tells.name: Focus outline removed
tells.summary: outline-none without a replacement focus style, so keyboard users cannot see where they are.

tells.name: No results that look like an empty list
tells.summary: A search or filter that matches nothing shows the same screen as a list with nothing in it, or gives no way to clear it, so people think their data is gone or get stuck.
